qmroot_binding.note: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only

description: Defines the formal model of structural trajectories through state-space over time. A trajectory is the transformation-grounded path of a structure S through successive configurations. This map covers trajectory definition, state-space representation, transformation grounding, trajectory types, and cross-book trajectory feeds. All trajectories are grounded by INV-PD-001 — every step must be bridged by a declared transformation.

components.S(t_i): The structural configuration of S at time-point t_i. A configuration is a full structural tuple ⟨N, R, C⟩ satisfying the Book 1 FFT primitives.
components.T: The transformation sequence ⟨τ_0, τ_1, ..., τ_{n-1}⟩ where each τ_i is a declared transformation mapping S(t_i) to S(t_{i+1})
components.time_points: t_0 < t_1 < ... < t_n — an ordered index of evaluation events. Time is discrete and evaluation-relative; it does not imply clock time.
components.trajectory_length: n — the number of transformation steps. A trajectory of length 0 is a fixed point (S = S(t_0) with no transformation applied).

trajectory_definition.structural_note: A trajectory is not a record of observed configurations — it is a structurally grounded account of how a pattern moved through state-space. The transformation record is the trajectory's structural backbone; without it, a sequence of configurations is a collection, not a trajectory.

state_space_model.title: Structural State-Space
state_space_model.definition: The state-space of a structure class Ξ is the set of all configurations reachable by applying declared transformations from any initial configuration S(t_0) ∈ Ξ.
state_space_model.formal: SS(Ξ) = { S' : ∃S ∈ Ξ, ∃τ ∈ declared_transforms*: τ*(S) = S' }
state_space_model.note: declared_transforms* is the reflexive-transitive closure of declared transformations — all configurations reachable in zero or more steps.

regions.label: Stable Region
regions.description: Configurations from which all trajectories converge to an attractor within a bounded number of steps. The stable region is the union of all attractor basins in SS(Ξ).
regions.pd_relevance: Trajectories entering the stable region are classified as convergent by PD-Τ and handed to PD-Β for attractor identification.

regions.label: Transient Region
regions.description: Configurations from which trajectories eventually enter the stable region but have not yet converged. Transient trajectories are the primary analysis domain of PD-Τ.
regions.pd_relevance: PD-Τ traces transient trajectory steps and logs each transformation. Transient length is a trajectory complexity measure.

regions.label: Bifurcation Boundary
regions.description: Configurations at the boundary between two or more attractor basins. Trajectories at the bifurcation boundary are sensitive to transformation parameters — small perturbations send them to different attractors.
regions.pd_relevance: Bifurcation boundary configurations are forwarded from PD-Τ to PD-Β immediately upon detection.

regions.label: Dissolution Region
regions.description: Configurations from which no declared transformation produces a valid successor configuration. Trajectories entering the dissolution region terminate — the pattern dissolves.
regions.pd_relevance: Dissolution region entry is a terminal trajectory event. PD-Τ records the final valid configuration and logs the dissolution event for the catalogue phase.

trajectory_types.label: Convergent Trajectory
trajectory_types.description: A trajectory that approaches and reaches an attractor within the state-space. Every configuration in the trajectory satisfies an increasing proportion of the attractor's invariant set, monotonically.
trajectory_types.formal: convergent(S, A) ⟺ ∀i: inv_match(S(t_i), A) ≤ inv_match(S(t_{i+1}), A)  and  lim_{i→n} inv_match(S(t_i), A) = 1
cross_book_instances: GRL authority decay trajectory converging to stable_authority attractor (α approaching steady-state) — feeds from GRL-Σ α_trajectory
SARG argument construction converging to valid argument attractor — feeds from SARG-Σ structural_argument_trajectory
OR revelation trajectory converging to fully_revealed state (ω → 0 under repeated observation)

trajectory_types.label: Divergent Trajectory
trajectory_types.description: A trajectory that moves away from all declared attractors. Divergent trajectories either reach the dissolution region or are intercepted by a bifurcation event that redirects them.
trajectory_types.formal: divergent(S) ⟺ ∀A ∈ attractors: inv_match(S(t_i), A) is not monotonically increasing
trajectory_types.pd_action: PD-Τ flags divergent trajectories for PD-Β bifurcation analysis. Divergent trajectory without a bifurcation event within a bounded window triggers dissolution logging.

trajectory_types.label: Cyclic Trajectory
trajectory_types.description: A trajectory that returns to a previously visited configuration after a finite number of steps. A cycle of length 1 is a fixed point. Cycles of length k > 1 are periodic orbits.
trajectory_types.formal: cyclic(S, k) ⟺ ∃i, j: i ≠ j ∧ j - i = k ∧ S(t_i) = S(t_j)
trajectory_types.nos_integration: Cyclic trajectories are structurally interesting under INV-NOS-003: the structure returns to a previous configuration, which is trivially identity-preserving. PD-Τ records the cycle length and the full cycle configuration sequence.

trajectory_types.label: Bifurcating Trajectory
trajectory_types.description: A trajectory that reaches a bifurcation point — a configuration from which two or more successor configurations are possible under the governing transformation. Bifurcating trajectories split into multiple continuation trajectories, each tracked independently.
trajectory_types.pd_action: PD-Τ detects the multi-successor condition and immediately transfers the configuration to PD-Β. PD-Τ suspends trajectory tracing until PD-Β returns the classified bifurcation event and the continuation trajectory assignments.

transformation_grounding.title: Declared Transformation Registry
transformation_grounding.requirement: Every trajectory step must reference a transformation from the declared transformation registry. The registry is populated at init phase from all eight upstream books.

registry_sources.transforms: FFT primitive transformations: structural union, relational product, constraint application, invariant assertion
IS topological transformations: center emergence, periphery reorganization, topological inversion
SD detection transformations: signature extraction, pattern matching, detection completeness evaluation
OR transformations: opacity measurement, revelation threshold crossing, latent structure access
TEL transformations: syntax check, semantic evaluation, composition, assertion
GRL transformations: regime validation, authority decay application, enforcement cycle, collapse
SARG transformations: argument construction, warrant mapping, defeat application, evaluation gate
NoS transformations: autonomy audit, realism classification, identity test, causation audit, synthesis

transformation_grounding.tel_encoding: All transformations are expressible in TEL via T[τ_i]: S(t_i) → S(t_{i+1}). TEL-Σ parse gate applies to all trajectory step encodings before PD-Τ records them.

cross_book_trajectory_feeds.pd_use: PD-Τ uses the cross_book_invariant_map as the initial state-space configuration at t_0. emergent_invariants_confirmed informs PD-Β attractor classification. upward_revisions_pending are tracked as trajectory perturbation events.

cross_book_trajectory_feeds.content: Authority measure time-series α(t_0), ..., α(t_k); decay_projection for next n enforcement cycles; collapse_risk_flag
cross_book_trajectory_feeds.pd_use: PD-Τ ingests the α_trajectory as a named sub-trajectory within the governance domain. decay_projection is used by PD-Β to project bifurcation event timing. collapse_risk_flag triggers immediate bifurcation boundary classification.

cross_book_trajectory_feeds.content: Sequence of argument configurations A(t_0), ..., A(t_m) across the SARG evaluation cycle; defeat events; evaluation gate outcomes
cross_book_trajectory_feeds.pd_use: PD-Τ traces the SARG argument trajectory as a pattern within argumentation state-space. Defeat events are registered as trajectory perturbation events; evaluation gate failures trigger bifurcation boundary detection.

steps.action: Initialize trajectory log with S(t_0) from the declared starting configuration or from the NoS-Σ cross_book_invariant_map
At each t_i, identify the applicable declared transformation τ_i from the transformation registry
steps.gate: If no τ_i bridges S(t_i) to any declared S(t_{i+1}): log gap event; classify as bifurcation candidate; transfer to PD-Β

steps.action: Apply τ_i and verify S(t_{i+1}) satisfies the transformation's post-condition
steps.tel_check: TEL-Σ parses the T[τ_i]: S(t_i) → S(t_{i+1}) expression; PASS required before recording the step

steps.action: Classify the step: convergent, divergent, cyclic, or bifurcating (see trajectory types)
If bifurcating: transfer to PD-Β. If dissolution: log terminal event and terminate. Otherwise: advance t_i → t_{i+1} and repeat from step 2
On trajectory completion (attractor reached, cycle detected, or dissolution): record full trajectory log and forward to PD-Σ for synthesis
